encounters are composed of just normal people i never had to adapt my playstyle to new threat and my monowire just shredded everything i never thought to experiment with new playstyle or weapon because nothing ever posed enough of threat even though the gameplay is subpar i just could not put it downthe main selling point is actually the massive and immersive open world you have to explore the world of night city feels incredibly realistic and itll take you forever to completely run out of things to do night city is so well put together that i didnt start using fast travel until i hit the 30hour mark i was constantly pulled into the experience and the illusion was almost never shattered and its not like exploration stops at generic future city the outskirts of the map include more suburban neighborhoods and vast desert with mobile camps and raiders if you enjoy exploration you will love cyberpunk the game even rewards you for walking around the world with unique encounters sidequests gear or just the simple ability to admire the scenery i personally recommend choosing to do side jobs more than gigs because theyre the more narrativefocused quests some of my favorite encounters were stumbling into cyberpsychos that were boss fights my favorites of the bunch involved dodging sniper in the open badlands and fighting someone in mechanical skeleton that fired laser beams i dont think anything else other than the story wouldve solidified my opinion on cyberpunk the writing in this game is one of the strongest ive seen in an openworld game from the main plot to the sidequests every piece of the english language found here is delightfully put together the characters were the strongest element for personally characters that were just talking cars and vending machines have more personality than 90 of video game characters johnny silverhand is the clear highlight as the deuteragonist but that is far from saying others never stood chance of competing with him the animations and voice acting do lot to sell these characters too the themes of the plot arent limited to the standard cliche cyberpunk ones as well its not revolutionary for the genre in that sense but i still think its highlight for this subsect of fiction i personally enjoyed that each of the games endings felt like satisfying conclusion to the plot in entirely unique ways its very rare for game to have multiple endings and for one of them to not be the good ending and i adore cyberpunk for that people are going to take away vastly different message from the game depending on what you choose in the final few moments httpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2925221345quick note the soundtrack is also really good been good to know new dawn fades and the rebel path are some of my favorites of the standard original bits but theres also large chunk of songs composed by johnnys band that are actually in the game never fade away is likely the most iconic of the bunch but its full album theres bunch of licensed music as well that you can listen to while drivingand theres something i feel that i probably dont have to mention but i feel inclined to while nowhere near as bad as its launch the game is still at bethesda level of quality when it comes to bugs while cyberpunk 2077 never crashed for i did get softlocked and experienced dozens of graphical bugs and technical glitches and for game that focuses so heavily on immersion this will pull you out of the experience every time it happens npcs faces wont load in until youve looked at ps2 model for few seconds my voice actor swapped genders for one scene only to immediately fix itself the next time i opened my mouth vehicles would float in the area on the regular one dialogue section at the very end of the game had character holding gun while using his tablet there were people tposing in the opening cutscene for s sake not only is this the patched version but this is also the pc version god help you if you played on last gen console while its amazing that the game is in playable state now it was unethical for the studio to release cyberpunk in the state that they did cyberpunk isnt labor of love out of passion its out of necessity cd projekt red shouldnt be applauded for doing the bare minimum and fixing broken product httpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2925219285cyberpunk 2077 is far from the best rpg out there its probably not even close to the best openworld game but it is one of the most immersive games with very compelling narrative that constantly pulls you in only for the hundredth bug to immediately pull you out while it wouldve made the game less glitchy i dont think any more time in the oven wouldve make it any better there was clear conflict of interest in what gameplay genre the developers wanted to make im personally giving the game 710 i think the people arguing that this game is one of the worst out there are dead wrong but its still far from what was promised and excluding the bugs and disastrous launch im ok with that

producto recibido forma gratuita maybe im getting little bit cynical these days but part of expected to be left with bad taste in my mouth after playing the elder scrolls v skyrim special edition generally thats what happens when companies try to milk every last cent out of an existing ip let alone game and all you have to do is look at the reviews for dlc packs of any number of franchises to see that many other people have the same feelings on this subject as i do zenimax have done something little different this time however and it changes up the tried and true method that they have used for almost fifteen years of releasing two or three expansions followed by goty edition six years after the original release skyrim is in fact hd remaster complete with 4k support and whole bunch of other very pretty thingsprobably the biggest reason that skyrim represents coup not only for zenimax but for the gaming industry as whole is that there is now very firm precedent for large studios to give owners of the full game these hd remasters for free on steam 2k studios did similar thing with the revisions of bioshock bioshock 2 and considering that bioshock and skyrim are possibly two of the biggest aaa titles to have been released ever i find it hard to imagine that other studios wont follow suit when releasing hd remasters in the future well except capcom but that situation is little different in some ways i guessthe main thing is that to be on the receiving end of such generosity for being loyal consumer is sadly something that very rarely happens in this day and age if it ever did in the first place with video games and rather than giving the internet another reason to criticise zenimax for not releasing another installment in the elder scrolls saga i for one have been humbled and galvanised in my resolve to wait patiently for what comes nextnone of the quest lines have been changed or updated in skyrim and there are extras in terms of content what is very interesting though is that the ability to apply official mods hosted by bethesdanet been added if you are member of bethesdanet you will be able to sign in download and apply skyrim mods all ingame so in that way huge amount of content essentially been added to the vanilla game its just that you get to make the choice what you do and dont want to included unfortunately however applying mods will disable your ability to unlock steam achievements this is pretty contentious point and there is understandably lot of discussion in the forums around the subject but im lucky enough to have already devoted hundreds of hours to the legendary edition and unlocked all the achievements i could be bothered doing so its biggie that i miss out this time i do think that it would be fairly simple matter to flag mods that change gameplay enough to warrant the disabling of achievements considering that all the mods are hosted by bethesda anyway and therefore make it little more fair for those who are purchasing this edition of skyrimas well as remastered art and effects skyrim also now boasts volumetric lighting also known as god rays as well as new snow and water shaders and updated screenspace reflections not only does this make the detail of individual models more appealing what i noticed more than anything was that it makes the vistas throughout skyrim far more epic than they already were looking up at high hrothgar from the gates of whiterun is enthralling sunrise over dawnstar breathes type of life and beauty into that town that it previously lacked running around the forest outside riften under full moon is absolutely captivating and combined with dynamic depth of field really brings the graphical standard of this game up to par with some of the really good work that is being done on other engines like unityif i didnt receive this game for free and i saw friend playing it i would be absolutely pulling my hair out trying to decide whether to buy it again the only thing that would stop is that its not combined with an expansion like hearthfire or dawnguard but if i had never played skyrim or any of the elder scrolls games before i would buy this game in heartbeat every single game in this series not including the mmo which i wont speak of here represents and amazing level of value in terms of money spent to gameplay provided while other longrunning franchises falter and fade the elder scrolls only gets better with time as an extra point of interest you should also check out the tesrenewal project where the community are working on rebuilding earlier games in the franchise for the modern engine very cool

that timenow at over 70 hours i literally only experienced one instance very early in my playthrough that resulted in needing to force and exit and reload previous save in order to progress vs link cable wasnt loading for the extraction point tutorial thus wouldnt trigger the exit following that hiccup there was some occasional popin with traffic and pedestrians with some questionably strategic vehicle popin during one chase mission and quite lot of npc cloning in some areas however none of those aspects were really enough to be outright distracting or diminish the overall beauty of this game and especially its ability to tell an engaging story the story is somewhat knowingly in the style of altered carbon as it relates to world building and central characters behaving authentically to the environment and their background the voice acting and motion capture paired with some of the most impressive textures ive ever seen in game work well together to add authenticity to the minor and pivotal moments there are some unexpectedly heartfelt moments especially when playing as female v and pursuing relationship with judy which results in one of my favorite moments in gaming and deliberate nod to radioheads pyramid song and video keanu reeves voice acting seems at times slightly incompatible with the context of some scenes but hes playing pretty unlikable character and anything off kilter about him smooths out as you progress to the final acts and even perhaps this is due to how the character exists in the game and how their personality develops throughout the players progressionthe combat and controls feel tight intuitive and there are wealth of perks to choose from such that there are few perks and fewer talents containing those perks that dont feel worthy of spending your points on the compatibility between quickhacking and stealth can at times take the challenge away from opting for combat centered approach though anything you can do to avoid the flatlining death screen is preferable in any event again looking beyond the micro and enjoying the macro this world and especially the level of detail that went into night city is absolutely splendid they embellished city that is advertising to its consumers at every corner whether its hypersexual or some massive hologram koi swimming above your head through glass dome as you speed down the highway daytime or nighttime cyberpunk consistently delivers on the visual wowfactor if you arent compelled to focus on game that didnt meet expectations on day 1 it certainly comes very close now in its current incarnation and close for those of us not completely spoiled by expecting perfection is still enough for this game to stand on its own as worthwhile bit of escapism i anticipate with ongoing patches the user experience with only be further enriched as for now its plenty rich and plenty playable id love to see cd projekt red have enough of reason to justify showing us more of this worldfyi i opted for streetkid played for the good ending with the aldecaldos support and one of my favorite missions centered around delamain the ai taxi company who had one alter that will sound very familiar from another popular franchise about all i can say without getting into spoilers

let preface this review by saying this is my first fromsoftware game i did my research however and i had pretty good idea of what i was walking into before i bought the game it does not disappointgameplaythis game is hard but you probably already know that so unless youre some sort of gaming god coming from the future youll die few times if youre like and this is your first fromsoftware experience youll die lotthat said dying in this game feels like part of the learning experience the more you play the game and find out about opponents patterns and weaknesses the less you find yourself looking at those dreaded red letters spelling your doom it embodies the good old git gud experience without being too punishing because it is an open world game but more on that lateroverall gameplay is amazing the controls are solid theres approximately million different ways to approach every situation and it feels very rewarding when you finally kill that boss thats been mopping the floor with you for the past thirty minutesgraphicsthis game is proof that you dont need the absolute latest and greatest top of the line graphics to look beautiful even though it doesnt have super mega detailed textures or raytracing like some other aaa games elden ring more than makes up for it with its art direction its absolutely flawless really everywhere you look the game not only looks stunning but it also makes sense everything is there for reason and it creates very cohesive aesthetic that just works every region its own quirks so places feel different from each other but at the same time theyre all held together by this consistent art direction work this game is gorgeous and the attention to detail never ceases to amaze even the paintings on the walls look great solid 55 heresoundsound is another big win for the soundtrack is 100 in tune with the rest of the game it pulls you in connects you to the world and kicks in when needed most of the time its very subtle yet very atmospheric tune but there are also some amazing compositions to be heard during boss fights i found myself listening to the soundtrack on its own just for funeverything else in sound design also makes sense and gives you clues on how to play the game small things like the sound when an enemy is killed or when you land critical attack are very satisfyingthe worldelden rings world is huge at the time of this review i still havent seen all of it but it is indeed giganticyoud think it gets repetitive and boring after while but theres always something new to see i find myself going back to places ive been before to do another round of exploring which by the way is easy to do thanks to the very convenient fast travel mechanic in the game and i end up finding stuff i missed the first time the world feels lived in and rewards you for exploringlike i said previously all areas of the map feel like their own little map because there are specific characteristics to each one but somehow the developers made it all work together it really is masterpiece in world designstoryon the story department theres few cutscenes here and there but for the most part the game doesnt tell you much about it leaving it up to you to find out if you want to through npcs items and the world itself speaking for myself theres still lot of things i dont understand about the story while i still havent finished the game i have feeling that it wont tell everything about the story without making go the extra mile and work for it personally im fan of storydriven narratives so i wouldnt mind having some more explanation on whats going on particularly on some parts of the gamereplay valueoof where do i start im 62 hours deep on two different saves so far they feel like different games thats how good the replay value is you can be mage you can be tanky guy swinging huge sword you can cast incantations and use magic weapons the options are endless you will play this game more than once and it will still feel fresh and new the second and probably third and fourth and fifth timebugsive had few frame drops and stuttering issues here and there and i died randomly once while climbing on my horse so while its not been completely flawless experience id say these are acceptable little bugs that the developers are working on btwis this game worth the money from first time fromsoftware player the answer is hell yeah it doesnt hold your hand it makes you work for it but it is extremely rewarding and comes wrapped in beautiful package with some of the best art direction ive ever seen in video game this is game for gamers buy it

ive now completed 2 full playthroughs and have over 200 hours in the game i have to say i like it anyone peripherally following the cyberpunk 2077 launch obviously heard of the bugs ai causing cars to randomly crash and explode items not spawning or despawning randomly items randomly falling or flying off when opening container jumping 10cm can sometimes kill you on landing some loot is just unlootable those are all real things that can still occur in the current patch 122 and you need to be aware of them before you take the plunge however the game does offer lot of good things the setting is great cyberpunks dystopian world is just amazing deep if youre into lore and background info the rabbit hole you can go down is insanely deep the story is interesting and the characters used have solid distinct personalities it is all presented in way which suits the dystopian setting well the game allows you fair amount of ways to play it you have different playstyles different combat approaches etc that said i often get bogged down into one way of playing being sneaky stealthy hacker it often looks visually stunning while performance is perfectly acceptable for at 1440p with most on high with rtx off only population density had to be kept at medium due to having fairly old i77700kbut even if i am fan of this game there are some severe let downs that i wish they would fix some of them dont even require whole lot of work the world is fairly stale and unreactive because your actions have little to impact for instance what you wear impact while the game allows you to dress like punk street trash and as high class corpo nowhere in game is this really taken into account posh wine bars will still call you scum from watson even if youre dressed in the most expensive corpo suits in the same fashion the reaction of gangs to your presence is generally unchanged even if youre known for wholesale slaughtering their friends only in few scripted quest events there are some reactions to your behavior the gangs in the cyberpunk world are supposed to be very diverse and they sure look the part with each their own distinctive look and voice lines however with the ncpd scanner jobs and gigs it is pretty much revealed that they all act the same way they all take part in the same criminal behavior i would really like to see some differences there to add flavor to the world maybe it allows you to feel more sympathy for some gangs and hate for others that said all gangs are obviously bad in their own way so even if you liked some your morals would still be challenged in what you deem acceptable behavior car ai is horrendous quite often cars crash during scripted dialogues and whatnot its not rare to see run down lighting poles and traffic lights all over the city the city also motorcycles on the road while you can find them parked almost anywhere i assume thats because the driving ai is so attrocious while the graphic design is often on point sometimes its clearly not well integrated together good example is the fact that during slowmotion your screen color shift thats nice effect except that it makes almost all red dots in game almost unusable in certain lighting conditions the game fairly large selection of clothes to sample during your playthrough but sadly it is very unlikely that youll be able to stick to the type of style which you prefer for your character the ability to find the right gear is fairly limited and largely depends on luck there are many stores but most serve limited style and them spawning the gear you wish to have with decent stats is rare occurrence finding stuff from drops is very happygolucky i suspect most gamers will only have seen tiny fraction of the options this game to offer in similar vain to the clothing styles above weapons and cars are also limited in choices skins and coloring can not be changed even if the world is fully of examples that are colored differently your corpo might be stuck with bright pink shotgun promoting the local strip club or your nomad might be forced to use gun with the logo of rival gang there is costumization for looks of car or weapon thats shame because all the assets are already ingameoverall id say that the witcher 3 succeeded better at creating an cohesive and immersive world even if its scope was more limited but cyberpunk 2077 is more than worth try if your pc can handle running it

one its own unique personalitythe quality of the main and sidequest is also mostly very good there are obviously some that are more memorable than others but lot of them are quite intriguing with some being really fantastichttpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2329649239visually the game is great as well night city itself with its neon lights advertisements everywhere and huge megablocks is crisis and the nerevarine prophecy was fulfilled skyrim is plunged into civil war and dragons have started to come back after thousands of years will you the dovahkiin dragonborn resolve the conflict and find out why the dragons are coming backwhere do you even start out with skyrim its such beloved game that even people outside of the gaming community know about it be it through friends or casual reference by other media and scarcely and day goes by where i dont get reminded of itskyrim continues the elder scrolls tradition of letting the player do whatever the hell they want matter how many times ive played through the game the sheer amount of content never fails to impress as the prophesied last dragonborn youll intervene on behalf of the native nords or the encroaching imperial legion from the third empire in an attempt to halt civil war youll also be directly responsible for preventing alduin the nordic god of destruction from obliterating the continent men women children and even tamriels omnipotent deities look to you for help to solve myriad of problems and troubles as result of the growing unrest as the player youre allowed the opportunity to tackle quests in particular order and because enemies scale as the character levels travel to different parts of the world can be done without fear of bumping into overleveled enemiesas roleplaying game youll assume the role of character of your own making selecting from number of different races which yield different interactions and physical traits its easy to waste hours perfecting the look of your orc breton or argonian skills and abilities such as magic and crafting evolve as they are performed allowing you to create truly unique identity this novel system offers previously unseen level of freedom in how you play the game tired of hacking and slashing monsters to bits switch your hand axes for magical spells and visit the college of winterhold for some magic schoolin bored of being paragon of virtue help kid murder his caretaker and join the ranks of the dark brotherhood most open world roleplaying games pigeonhole you into specific roles and lock content behind archetype requirementsim surprised that theres not that many games that follow this kind of trend of having large open world with guilds main quests side quests and not only that but supported by rich lore and deep world buildingin my opinion the elder scrolls franchise one of the best universes that you could spend so much hours reading into that can only be compared to that of tolkiens works but unfortunately is dismissed by most people as just medieval fantasy rpg i cant quite explain how vast the world is beyond tamriel all i can say about the lore is that its definitely worth delve into as knowing about the snow elves and how they devolved into the falmer makes exploring their caves much creepier or about the secrets of the dwemer as you wander the eerily empty halls that used to house thousands of dwarves making the world feel alive and filled with history even without you in itskyrim doesnt care about you its place that exists in its own right and you interact with it however you see fit thats what makes it such coherent believable world and thats skyrims enduring appeal its place where you escape to where you define your own character according to the decisions you make both physically within the game and mentally in your own head not the ones that are forced upon you and yes its land where its perfectly ok for hardened warriors to furiously crush the bones of bunnies if thats what they decide to refresh rates that high ive had problems with limiting my framerate to 100 via rivatuner the framerate is rock solid too for apart from the games intro sequence it rarely drops below 95 or so and game from dangerous and scary adam smasher to soothing and routine judy applies to the ingame street ads everything ever so slightly related to the samurai band later about that and clothing for the prettier the sights you see while driving through the city at night are worth lot by itself 3 the characters each and every from the main character cast is very memorable and well written whenever johnny and yes the trope with the iconic character that only the protagonist can see due to said characters being inside their head is as old as the world examples arkham knight tales from the borderlands appears and starts talking about his terrorist past or just says something disturbing in general you cant help yourself but feel like hes all for real hes just that much of an idealist and you grow to love him for that at least thats the case with you either love johnny to bits or hate his guts inbetween from what ive heard but even the secondary characters like takemura and rogue are to be remembered and have countless things and unique character features to cherish them for 4 side missions just as rich if not even richer as the main story campaign while some of them are lackluster and unapologetically short quest lines such as dream on and the story of convicted murderer wanting to make difference through his newly acquired faith are going to stay with you for long long time all of the secondary quests related to samurai and silverhands past are also win the bickering between the former band members feels like those are the conflicts that couldve easily happened between any of the days of glory longtime passed rock bands be it say metallica or deep purple really authentic 5 the story yes as simple as that i really liked the main story of the game and the way it was flowing full of memorable encounters and events its the meat of the game and keeps you invested throughout written beautifully 6 the symbolism if you as silly as it sounds question yourself what makes human different from god wonder about afterlife and are curious about when does ones life truly end thats the right game to feast on the themes of faith yes faith not religion please never ever mix them together are touched very authentically in one of the sidequests too 7 audio and music the original soundtrack is perfect fit for this world from the menacing and grim v and consumer cathedral to the banging midtempo roller of the rebel path radio music is also great curated by the likes of run the jewels nina kraviz and grimes the latter contributed an absolutely stunning delicate weapon exclusively for the game too easily my favorite from all of the originals from cyberpunk 2077 the meh 1 gameplay yes as sad as it is the game gets little boring to play after while which is cardinal for game like this vehicles feel just okay the gunplay is borderline alright and the quickhack system is fun for while until you realize it was done better even in the first watch_dogs game only the story and the characters kept interested in immersing myself in more of the repetitiveness 2 customization yes sure you can customize your character to oblivion but thats about it you cant even change their haircut later on the clothing system is revolving purely around the stats and will force you to wear things you dislike for that sweetsweet combat advantage cars cant be customized whatsoever but luckily i never really cared about them in the first place but i have to admit that the game really allowed to shape and make my character exactly the way i want them to be even though if you cant be nonbinary in 2077 which i assume you cant since everyone keeps referring to you as to or she exclusively and the game doesnt really give you third option cdpr are i really enjoyed this game im fan of froms games so while i was confident theyd make an good game i was worried that the move to an open world format would diminish some of their other strengths i think instead they were able to show new strengths creating an open world that will be new standard by which to compare others going forwardthe gameplay is much like other from games though i did appreciate the effort they made to make it more varied and even in their own way make it more accessible through additional gameplay options between the many new options in this game like spirit summons and the resurrect ability in sekiro you can tell from been looking at ways of giving players alternative methods to overcome the difficulties in their games in smart ways that dont compromise their design and arent bland difficulty slider that changes the game globally pvp seems to have improved featurewise however the times i have played it i found it to suffer from lot of lag its hard to tell if this is caused by players or the game but its extremely common and makes pvp less enjoyable than it could bei found the bosses to be overall easier than in previous games with some notable exceptions where it seemed from was almost making point to show they can still make hard as hell boss fight when neededthe world design makes incredible use of scale and the areas have good amount of variety both in terms of types of environment but also in terms of the enemies within and the content density the first few areas are packed with places to explore and things to find while some of the latter areas are bit more sprawling and sparse i didnt care for some as much as others like the blinding snowfield but with so much thats bound to be the case the enemy variety is worth noting too someone recently counted them up and found that elden ring had more enemy types than breath of the wild ac valhalla ghost of tsushima and horizon forbidden west combinedthe emphasis on open world does mean bit of step down in terms of the small scale level design many of the past games dark souls 1 in particular is renowned for its incredible interlocking vertical layered approach to the world elden ring does have bit of this in spurts in areas the community taken to calling legacy dungeons but not quite to the same extent the graphics are huge step up in quality for from basically look at any screenshot of the landscape and it would probably make an amazing wallpaper from always had good artistic eye for presenting the player with interesting focal scenes and having an open world just allowed them to do that all the more characters designs are largely the same as past games passable but not their strong suit particularly with the faces and as ever the character creator is very difficult to work with perhaps even the hardest boss in the gamethe ui is very much from software ui there are some quality of life improvements like sorting and some better presentation of information but it is what it isthe armor is very cool but for all the variety i kept hoping there would be more maybe its case where theres just never enough but knowing how big of deal fashion is i keep hoping theyll lean into it more the armor alteration system is interesting but it almost feels like it wasnt fully fleshed out as in most cases with some notable exceptions its just about removing the cloak in the future at the least it would be nice to see color palette changes as an additional optionas far as the lore of the world goes this is probably the best realization of froms style of presenting lore in the abstract but discernable through the world and items you find and the lore of this world is very interesting to learn about as you go through the gamequests are bit of mixed bag i enjoyed the content of the quests such as there is im not opposed to froms typical minimalist quest design from tends to not treat quests as traditional rpg quests but more as fleeting ephemeral experiences with characters and things you do in the world may or may not advance your relationship with them much like life i get that however there is also good argument to be made that its still game at the very least if youre going this route with system where the conditions for advancement are not transparent then you need those quests to be reliable flexible and bug free and i feel like in the games current state this is lackingmany times there are quests that behave in unexpected ways or only via exceedingly strict conditions for instance i had one quest that would not advance until i had rested at one specific site of grace other site of grace would do and this one was not obviously associated with the events i had another case where bug preventing character from speaking with that had spending time trying to figure out what i was missing fortunately this was fixed in patch 104i kind of wonder if lot of the nonmainline quest content was added at the very end of development and thats the cause of these issues i get that feeling because even as of the most recent patch new stages to quest chains are still being added which is pretty unusual unfortunately combined with the previous issues this also leads to problems there is one new quest line with new character announced in the patch notes that i am unable to even begin because of nonquest related action that i took before they were added to the game in short im open to the way from designs quests but i think they fell short of what they were going forultimately these complaints dont detract from the overall experience which is still pretty amazing i highly recommend this game and look forward to future dlc

the beginning of 2023 i started playing the game with low expectations and to my surprise i freakin loved itnever fade awayi think the theme and worldbuilding of the game are its strongest points the game does an excellent job of presenting night city as city full of disasters where even the smallest mistake could end with your dead body in landfill and nobody gives the various affiliations such as the evil corporations that control the world with technology healthcare and even military services the street kids and their gangs like valentinos with their chicano culture the voodoo boys with their technological version of haitian voodoo or 6th street who wants to see nusa great again nomads like aldaceldos who reject the shiny walls scrappers and the dreams that the city to offer instead cling to their family valuesthe game convincingly showcases the consequences of these affiliations in every aspect of the world whether it be economic political or spiritual its clear that the developers did their homework on the cyberpunk universe and brought it to life in remarkable way much like the witcher seriesa like supremei somehow managed to avoid major spoilers for year and i was very pleased with the main story v and johnnys struggle with their identities blend of fight club and matrix is in fine line between multiple personality disorder schizophrenia and depersonalization it is fascinating to see v die and be reborn as new person both literally and figuratively to the realities of night city and work through their issues with johnny who is completely different persona legend of the past the balance between side jobs world events and main jobs arent as smooth as i expected it to be despite playing the game without taking long break i had trouble with connecting with some of the characters or understanding their motivations for certain actions it is most likely designed around the main story and main side jobs which are included in endingsthree specific side jobs stood out to and showed the games potential the sinnerman questline with stephenson former criminal who turns to religion and is exploited by the evil corp for crucifixion instead of death sentence is an incredibly engaging and provided emotional tension throughout the quest the second is rivers questline about an ordinary nypd officer whose nephew is kidnapped by man who brainwashes lost teenagers into becoming cyberpunk versions of what you would call humanbroodstock lastly theres peralezs questline about an honest politician who is unknowingly controlled by corporations due to injected false memories and how they become paranoid and lose everything over time these three side quests share one big commonality theyre grounded in reality and have relatable approach even though the technology and the instruments of the are different overall i like the main story and i feel like they did not use all the potential they had in many aspects of the game the majority of the side jobs feel uninspired but there are hints of what could have been better im hopeful for improvement with the upcoming dlcs and sequelchippin inthe gameplay is intriguing with the possibility to test out different builds and optimize your cyberwave to handle everything the city throws at youfor example you can use sandavista like martinez in the anime and turn into glorious katanawielding solo merc be knifethrowing or pistoleer assassin that prefers quiet stealthy approach like thief as takemura calls it or you can go full netrunner basically cyberpunk variant of mage and perish everyone by just hacking them over their own security cameras unfortunately it gets stale repetitive quickly and you realize that the many builds out there to discover is mere illusion even though it can be enhanced to some point by mods just like the plot i see great potential in the combat and build systems but it is definitely not implemented in complete wayside activities such as nypd announcements and gigs turn into mindless repetitive activities after short time despite my efforts uncover their story through the messages and objectives given by the fixers they just turned into various chores to get 100 completionits been over year since its release but there are still persistent bugs that sometimes require loading previous quick save the bugs didnt ruin my gameplay but it forces the player to take frequent quick saves to prevent any gameplay errorsthe general consensus that the game being unfinished is mostly applies to the gameplay and i agree on that it is enjoyable but definitely not polished enougharchangelin conclusion cyberpunk 2077 is game that the potential to be classic in the gaming world but it falls short due to its incomplete gameplay repetitive side activities lingering bugs and its take on the side stories despite these issues the game is still enjoyable and worth playing especially for those who are fans of openworld games or interested in the futuristic theme yet again i believe that the gameplay in the witcher series was not outstanding either but it was the unique theme setting and compelling stories that turned it into legendary piece i hope to see similar emphasis on storytelling in cyberpunk which would make it even more captivatingthe narrative character development and worldbuilding are highlights of the game and it was fun journey that i spent hours and hours on i definitely recommend it

skyrim was the easiest of the elder scrolls games to pick up for those unfamiliar with the franchise and that been my experience normal mode provides some challenge but should be easily surmountable by those who play lot of adventure games bethesda andor elder scrolls veterans however will probably want to bump up the difficulty the difficulty slider can always be adjusted on the fly so this is wish to invest in it the game is eminently replayable and the community created countless mods with which to tweak the game i recommend you at least take glance at the most popular ones even vanilla content feels meaningless life paths have effect on what actually happens in the story and merely offers you different prologue or some lines in conversation that again have impact on the actual game loot similar issues where for you find yourself wearing skirt power scouter and bandana because they offer 10 points more armour than the kevlar vest youve been wearing for the last 3 hours this fromsoftware said hey weve never done an openworld rpg i guess we can take whack at it then they delivered the best game of the genre in over decade perhaps ever everything i dislike about modern owrpg games is gone from miyazakis masterpiece other aaa games just keep copying the success of skyrim but having bigger and bigger maps with wide open level design 1000 map markers telling you exactly where to go and what to do at all times and combat systems that are generally pretty lackluster and simpleelden ring shatters all of those contrivances with fresh approach the world of elden ring is admittedly massive but unlike other games in recent memory corner of this map ever feels empty or boring the level design is lightyears ahead of most open world games verticality labyrinthine platforming and environmental puzzles are back on the menu after being abandoned by the hundreds of skyrim clones this past decade the legacy dungeons as they are known here are on par with the best of fromsofts dark souls series which is famous in part due to its long track record for stellar level designthe combat system and character customization are familiar for fans of fromsofts previous entries but in the new context of the ow genre it feels better than it ever the addition of jumping mechanics simple but satisfying mounted combat and exploration and heavily customizable weapon skill system compliment the play style of huge game like this weapon balance been bit shaky since the launch of er but recent patches have helped every playstyle feel satisfying and powerful without sacrificing the challengespeaking of difficulty this game is difficult more difficult than people unfamiliar with the developer would expect from game of this genre but not quite as difficult as the more punishing examples from other soulslike games the game does not hold your hand or litter your map with dozens of quest markers and points of interest if your map is marked its because an npc just told you that they would mark your map or youve just discovered new fast travel point the game subtly guides you to the next major objectives through unobtrusive visual cues and contextanother way the game accomplishes this task is by avoiding the shortcut most developers take to level the challenge to the players current level elden ring allows you to go wherever you want to go but if you enter an area that you are not supposed to yet then you will be punished by 15 foot tall hyena beasts giant demon crows and plagued wolves that will bleed you out in seconds you will either naturally gravitate back toward the areas appropriate to your level or you will rise to the punishing difficulty and be appropriately rewarded for your determination every area feels rewarding discovery is an element that is difficult to get right even in some of the best ow games ever made the lazy answer to reward exploration is to create 200 collectible items hidden in obscure locations that award trophies or minor character progression elden ring makes genuine exploration feel rewarding nearly every time somehow they have significant secrets hidden nearly everywhere if you spend 5 or 10 minutes striking out into the unknown you are almost certain to find sexy loot secret dungeon an interesting enemy or npc etc but none of it feels like hooray you found your 147th korok seeda few points of criticism are the performance issues that have been present since the launch despite having graphics that feel more like they were released late last generation there is some persistent stuttering even in the most powerful rigs so consistent 60 fps can be bit elusive while the art direction and style are phenomenal as always the graphics themselves are bit dated this is most likely due in part to the long development of the game and partly due to fromsoft insisting on using their same old engine instead the newer options some long time fans may find the gameplay systems to be rehash of soulsborne and have heard some fans say that they wanted more variation this time around i personally do not agree with this take as ive played every single fromsoft game since demons souls on opening day and elden ring did not strike as stale but i do understand why some would see it this wayi see these drawbacks as very minor in the greater scheme of this game and they do not take anything away from the spectacular execution on virtually every level of game design though i may be slightly biased in favor of fromsoft if i am trying to have modicum of objectivity i am comfortable saying that i think elden ring is one of the best openworld games of the last 15 years in the same tier as the likes of skyrim breath of the wild and the witcher 3 however my more subjective view is that this is likely my favorite game of all timeeither way this game is an easy 1010

i know im quite late to the review party and everything under the sun already been both praised and scrutinized on this game however as selfproclaimed cp2077 fanboy that rode the hype train and even built my latest gaming rig to prepare for its launch yes even scoring rtx 3080 in time i feel compelled to write out my thoughts long post ahead i originally wrote more but steam an 8000 character limit bahmy first impressions massive absolutely breathtaking the first time you step foot inside night city its simply marvel to behold sprawling concrete jungle that assaults your senses with neon signs beckoning you to spend and consume the sounds and sights are very atmospheric various districts reflect the people that work and live there for example the corporate sector everyone is mostly dressed to impress from business corpos to the lavishly lifestyled other areas are more worn down grungy swirling with smog and dust gangs transients invalids and generally povertystricken folks are more prominent here industrial sectors spit out flames from their towers autonomous machinery echoing in the distance making you wonder what cybernetic creations are being built the badlands desert area is an interesting contrast to the bustling city life barren wasteland smattered with nomad clans bloodthirsty gangs and rolling sandstorms the denizens of nc are also fairly varied in shape size and cybernetics it really feels like fully functional cyberpunk city high tech and low life the main plot is fairly interesting and the inclusion of keanu reeves as johnny silverhand was nice touch the main characters you interact with are also pretty realistic looking and are animated well the story missions are decent enough however my major gripe is with all of the side content in the way it was presented lot of them involve characters just straight up bombarding you with calls when you get near certain locations you will get spammed lot and its very jarring they became bit of chore between running around waypoints and fast travel stations it was like i was playing skyrim at times rather than cdpr title the missions really needed to be more organic in nature the playstyles in this game are varied enough that it caters to most peoples tastes you can spec into guntoting maniac like and just slaughter enemies mercilessly like the terminator you can become hacking prodigy and fry the eyeballs right out of someones head stealth it up with ninja sword whatever you want its likely there there are also 3 main lifepaths that determine your backstory but they dont affect the games story much if at all you get wide selection of weapons to use ranging from traditional guns and knives to tech weaponry that uses different perks such as autoaim some weapons like turrets can only be used if you have the right perk i would have hoped for few more kinds of weapons but for the most part these do the job well if there ever was huge variety of something in this game it would likely have to be clothing there is an overwhelming selection of wearables to choose from however as is the problem in most rpgs you will often be seeking out the items with the best stats in turn if youre relying on loot which is usually the case this means your character will look like complete freak at times sport coat shiny yellow baggy pants cowboy boots and trilby hat oh boy if you go with your fashion sense instead youll get nice looking character that will practically die when the wind blows as the game progresses youll find enough loot that it will become easier to find the look you want as well as the armor but early game its hot mess they really should have included an option that some rpgs include where you can change the appearance of something you like to the stats of another item basically adopting the look but retaining the stats theres also great selection of cars and bikes to choose from many of which you can buy and own theyre very detailed inside kudos to the art team on this and you can listen to various radio stations that said the music is fairly varied but familiar enough to relate to metal glam rock rap latino techno etc unfortunately you cant own all of the cars in the game and even worse you can not modify them either this was rumored to be one of many planned features that got cut short due to time constraints hopefully it will be available in future dlc one aspect of the game i really need to gush over is the photo mode this is by and far the new gold standard for games that include this mode there are ton of options you can use to tweak photos different filters backgrounds stickers posesi probably spent about half my time ingame with this mode and ive taken 300 screenshots i really hope that other games take note of this robust system and incorporate something similar its an absolute blast performance and stability this is where it gets rather ugly theres hiding it this game is chock full of issues even 4 months after release i know lot of people are still having issues with getting decent fps rates on this game for game thats supposed to run better frames on rtx and dlss i fail to see it im running core i9 10850k 49ghz with 32gb ram rtx 3080 with all settings maxed and yet i still cant hit 60fps at times mostly it likes to run in the 50s but sometimes dips down to the high 30slow 40s i cant even imagine how it runs on lower rigsand the bugsoh man i think the longer i played the game it got worse to the point that it almost prevented from finishing the game near the end most of them werent too bad such as visual glitches but others would get stuck on objects or just get killed instantly from doing something like hopping onto counter despite multiple delays i believe cdpr just didnt have enough time to fix anything the devs were pressured by corporate to push out the product before christmas 2020 and this was the unfortunate end result another gripe i have most of the game is all style substance theres lot to behold with the sights and the details the game oozes atmosphere but theres nothing to enjoy if you want to roleplay within it the more you play the more your heart sinks when you notice the amount of features that dont exist npcs interact with odd responses that dont even qualify as typical generic ones i cant sit on bench or stool and buy noodle bowl or whatnot hundreds of doors that say locked and cant be opened arcade games that cant be played i cant even sleep on my bed properly sleeps sideways off the side of the bed you are given world to play around in but theres sand in the sandbox for something so painstakingly well made in terms of detail it hurts to know that you cant truly be part of it final thoughts ultimately i really enjoyed the game it wasnt quite what i expected from all the hype though the amount of bugs and missing content really cut short the potential it had it could have been so much better and would have benefitted from another delay of at least 6 months to year although i have played games that were much much worse than this ill definitely play this again as i need to finish my 100 achievement run but i will wait until the game is patched up and ideally once all the dlc is released despite the many flaws it had it still was phenomenal experience i enjoyed my stay in the dystopian future that is night city cruel place where nobody wins and there are truly happy endings sometimes thats just how life is and i can appreciate good game that reflects that endless thanks to the talented dev team for their hard work i hope to see more of the cyberpunk 20xx series in the future

edition so named because ordinary remaster doesnt sound quite so appealingin terms of content this is exactly the same game as was released in 2011 albeit with all the subsequent dlc included from the start it seen graphical upgrade though the details of which well get into in moment there is also mod support available from launch which on the playstation 4 in particular been long time comingalthough its taken for granted nowadays the transition of the elder scrolls from niche franchise to mainstream hit was great surprise at the time before 2006s oblivion the idea of western roleplaying game being one of the most successful games of the year wouldve been laughed at and yet its popularity paved the way not just for skyrim but the mainstream acceptance of the likes of dragon age and the witcherthe elder scrolls success is doubly surprising given the rather bland tolkienesque fantasy world the games are set in although its lack of distinguishing features made it easier for bethesda to create more grounded experience for skyrim that doubt helped to attract more casual interest each game is named after particular location in the world with skyrim being nordicinspired land of horned warriors and snowy mountainsas the game starts your character who can be customised from any number of humanoid races been mistakenly rounded up with bunch of prisoners rebelling against the games continentspanning empire youre later able to join either side if you wish but the rights and wrongs of the situation are not at all clear cut your initial consideration though is that youre about to be beheaded and are only saved by ruddy great dragon attacking the village youve been brought toit transpires that dragons havent existed in the world for centuries and their appearance is supposed to augur the apocalypse naturally you turn out to be the chosen one that can stop them dragonborn who is able to learn their language and absorb their powerthis is all very exciting at the time but once you escape from the dragon the real appeal of skyrim is made clear youre given some advice that you should head to nearby village for help but if you dont want to theres nothing at all stopping you from ignoring the story for the rest of the game and just heading off to explore on your own you can become mercenary learn craft or buy house and find spouse its entirely up to you and the game encourages any and every eventualityit doesnt entirely abandon you though and if it thinks youve got lost itll start pointing you in the direction of story quest locations although give theres over 200 dungeons to explore the chances of you not happening across something on your own are remotealthough there is third person option the first person view is the default which means the basics of combat are kept as simple as possible the left trigger controls whatevers in your left hand the right whatevers in your right there are few context sensitive actions depending on what they are spells needed to be powered up while theres basic block and counter system for shields but it means you can instantly get stuck in whether youre wielding twohanded battleaxe or fireball and healing spellsgiven the detailed upgrade system and your ability to craft your own weapons armour and potions this is true roleplayer in way youd never expect of such mass market game but bethesda game studios main weakness continues to be dialogue and character interaction the amateur hour voiceovers which range from nordic brogue to californian twang are constantly distracting although the dialogue they mangle is so full of cliché its not as if theyre ruining anythingand despite the move to the playstation 4 the games human characters still look like woodcarved puppets with robotic animation that would often shame playstation 2 game the visuals for the games landscapes are more impressive though especially as you know everything you see from the highest snowcapped mountain to the low marshland is real location that can be travelled to and exploredin terms of improvements for the special edition the frame rate is locked at 30 frames per second with 1080p resolution the draw distance noticeably extended in terms of adding in extra background details like foliage and theres new depth of field effects shadows look more realistic and so too does snow ice and running water theres also lot of use of the god rays that so often ground fallout 4s far harbor dlc to halt although theyre much less problematic here in fact the performance is all round very good with almost slowdown and relatively few bugsparticularly compared to the original playstation 3 release the difference is night and day and yet the special edition is still only emulating the original pc version with maxed out graphics that means its still well behind the pace of modern games especially when compared to conceptually similar titles like the witcher 3 its still the terrible animation and unnaturally static landscapes that you notice before any of the improvements as welcome and as wellimplemented as they are but to do any more wouldve involved remaking the game almost from scratch and wed much rather bethesda work on new game than spend too much time on an old oneafter all its not just the visuals that are showing their age but also the simplistic quest design and to skyrim and bethesda have clearly put lot of effort into this special edition even if it is almost as if theyre fighting losing battle with new content though weve desire to play all 100 hours all over again even if were sure many will although of course if youve never played the game at all then this represents incredibly good value for money but for us the main thing we took away from skyrim irreplaceable seconds of existence forever lost to alduins fanged maw and todd howards malignant dreams of global dominion and yet i regret none of it not one pointless unproductive minute and given elden ring elden ringwhere to begin with this one fromsoftwares journey from demons souls in 2009 all the way to here leaves us in the incredible foundations of what could be considered their best game yet utilising the familiar soulsborne format while spinning it into fullfledged open world the game is utterly jam packed with things to discover fight and oddball characters with weird esoteric stories and motives game with an insane vision and incredible imaginationhaving finished it about 160 hours in my expectations probably should have been tempered context time ive beaten almost every game in fromsoftwares modern lineup with the exception of demons souls due to not owning ps3 or ps5 ive gone out of my way to seek the greatest challenges from charmlessdemon bell runs in sekiro to the queen yharnam trophy in bloodborne elden ring starts off not too dissimilar to dark souls 3 and will seem incredibly familiar from there with the magic meter returning along with split healingmagic bar flasks and its weapon arts exchanged for new system called ashes of war allowing you to chop and change various skills into variety of mundane weapons creating entirely brand new playstyles and strategies magic is stronger than ever with spell slots being completely independent of the stat that increases your magic bar actively encouraging you to seek out magic to use this makes the games first stretch incredibly replayable as you experiment with various ashes and spell and weapon combinations that compliment each other even better is that exploration from your first playthrough is rewarded in the next as you can skip surprising number of bosses and encounters to find strong equipment or spells early and use it as base for your new run this is some of the best character building in any of these games and the world never stops being absolutely breathtaking to look at and experienceunfortunately it seems elden ring eventually buckles under its ambitions in an attempt to top what came before it the game is relatively challenging from limgrave all the way up to past the altus plateau and leyndell the royal capital and then skyrockets in difficulty in recognising that the game to somehow challenge dozens of different player character builds and hundreds of potential ash of war combinations it becomes what might be fromsoftwares hardest game ever put to code what were once difficult bosses are now reused as regular enemies with impunity input reading is rampant gank bosses are common place enemies are sekirobloodbornetier aggressive with staggered combos and extreme delays and areaofeffect attacks in game where you play as relatively slow dark souls 3 character lategame healthpools are absolutely titanic difficult to stance break and even characters with high damage numbers begin to struggle without help from summons bleed or frostbite especially bleed given its status proc that scales infinitely matter how big the healthbarthe open world format both benefits and hurts the game because almost all of its good design is in 6080 of its runtime with the last two areas being gauntlet of less than five of the absolute hardest bosses in the game by the time i was done with those monsters four of which i could not at all beat without the help of certain extremely strong spirit summon i was fatigued and incredibly tired rather than feeling accomplished at all my advice is to play as dirty as humanly possible if youre struggling with those its life or death battle after alldespite those few hitches just before an absolutely fantastic ending id say elden ring is still worth your money and time if you can spare either dont go in expecting anything other than another dark souls this time with some of the words switched around and much bigger and youll have grand time of it

upon booting up elden ring youre immediately given glimpse of what is to come through the brilliant soundtrack starting off with few disparate calm strings the main theme slowly morphs into an epic melody of grandeur valor and unrelenting ambition despite having already heard this track in trailers i was blown away shattered even i knew i was in for something special blissful explorationwhereas previous soulsborne titles had you trudging through claustrophobic sewers and maddening towns elden ring is far bigger more ambitious adventure reaching across numerous regions the lands between are massive and filled with things to discover even after 20 hours i was still finding new things in the first area perhaps i had missed cave tucked away in canyon or failed to peruse nearby forest once i even stumbled upon an expansive underground area that you could easily miss its magical really much of the wonder comes from the design ethos gone are the myriad of question markers and intrusive quest logs you would find in other titles instead replaced by something as simple as your own curiosity fromsoftware uses this as tool to compel you forward when you see fort in the distance you will feel urged to go there and the best thing is that it was you and not the game that decided so elden ring relies on your participation and i love that httpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2790286880as you traverse these lands its hard not to be impressed by the topography uneven hills and deep gorges combine to create world that can not simply be navigated by holding down your left joystick its gargantuan structures serving not just to undermine you but also as waypoints on your journey it made realize how flat and easygoing the landscapes in open worlds often are in the lands between even the geography is your adversary constantly bending and defying rules my first 30 hours with elden ring were some of the best ive had in gaming and i was ready to name it fromsoftwares magnum opus but then realization dawned wait havent i seen this church beforethere are many reasons to love the soulsborne titles but one of them is the handcrafted quality that permeates throughout every corner of the world feels like it was designed with specific purpose in mind one that you would probably understand through your ponderings and each encounter offered new challenge these were games that not only encourage you to explore but also feature enough secrets to warrant doing so this still rings true here but for every two surprises there was moment of utter disappointment reused structures and bosses are frequent to the point where every foe not overtly important to the narrative will be fought multiple times it also undermines the sense of discovery since you can only happen upon so many identical dilapidated churches before you wonder if its worth it this is truest for the many dungeons and caves they all have the same visual identity and rarely differ in terms of enemies and i have hard time naming just one of them since they all blend into one large portion of copypaste tedium eventually i began looking at these as optional bonus levels rather than integral parts of the world and honestly i think that is the best approach it is also in this repetition that the developers misunderstand what made their bosses so special in the first place like telling joke these encounters require careful buildup harrowing walk through town gone mad or slowly making your way up castle the bosses were never the main attraction they served as final sendoffs stages of thrilling and heartpounding action to juxtapose the relatively quiet exploration this still applies to the linear locations but once you step into the open world miyazaki starts hurling bosses at you like hes kid training for sports match thats not to say the boss fights are bad when you come across one of the more sophisticated fights and composer yuka kitamura starts sending symphonic shockwaves through your ears this game is delightful with few exceptions the mandatory encounters are consistently astounding and satisfyingly grueling rounded off by exquisitely rich and repulsive visual design these moments are truly special httpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2790285862elden ring keeps on going just when you think youve seen it all it turns out theres still another half of the story left had it featured enough content to sustain this length it couldve been monumental achievement unfortunately that is not the case theres an entire region where the only unique foe is the boss at the end the rest being awkwardly recycled enemies and one of the best places in the game suffers from similar issueyet i cant help but love elden ring for weeks i was enthralled by its world and when i wasnt playing it i was thinking about where to explore next or how to approach the boss i was stuck on when i present these criticisms of the game its not because i despise it its because i care had this been disappointment i wouldve just shrugged and thought little more of it beauty and hostilitythrough the lands between fromsoftware toys with an interesting dichotomy while the landscapes are gorgeous and downright breathtaking they are far from safe mercenaries in tattered armor oversized crustaceans draconian soldiers the size of giants and even living jars everyone and everything is out to kill you even if there arent many enemies specific to one region there are still plenty of creative enemy designs the open world also gives you lot of freedom in how you approach these you could sneak your way through an enemy camp get up close and personal with comically large greatsword or ride in on your horse slashing wildly at anyone in your way this makes the notorious difficulty far more approachable and id imagine that more people will finish the game because of it the combat system itself is akin to dark souls 3 but there are enough additions to make it not feel worn out and dreary sekiros posture system where an enemys stance can be broken to leave them vulnerable been subtly integrated the enemies dont have wavering stamina bars over their heads but this means you arent pressured into style of play the stance mechanic is there you can use it if you want but it can also be ignored entirely httpssteamcommunitycomsharedfilesfiledetailsid2790286283when combined the stance system and guard counter result in battles coming across more as duels than the old hitandrun affair there were times where i had to run away either to heal or get break from the heat of battle but i spent considerably more time facing my enemy headon you could argue that not enforcing these improvements leads to some players resorting to the triedandtested tactics but i like the freedom it brings another enemy you will face is the performance while the game runs at 60fps most of the time there are some drastic problems with frame pacing and stuttering i didnt find it too distracting but those on lowerend pcs might be more affected its hard not to compare elden rings selection of enemies and locations to previous fromsoftware offerings but part of believes we should look at it through different lens for while it is like these in certain departments its also title that seeks to provide different experience one much more flexible in its design contours and of much grander scale rather than scold it for the ways it compares we should appreciate it for the ways it differs visit cup of the writing on the tin says dark souls but open world and you get exactly what it says on that tin give or take few quirks and its rare case of an openworld conversion done rightthe combat is the same old soulsborne system that youve already made your mind up about whether you like or not with some extra tweaks for variety but what elden ring really excels in is the open world of exploration it wraps it in strong art direction coupled with intruiging writing make for sights worth seeing and the reward loop for exploring is borderline addictive every single little cave camp crevasse and keep its own boss and unique item as reward for beating it making for ludicrously large assortment of builds to go for this of course comes with the standard high difficulty attached but in practice the spikes of hardship make for satisfying goals to work towards via levelingthere are other sharp edges however that youll need to acclimate to in bit of have your cake and eat it design youll be showered with lots of weapons but youll still need to stick to one and upgrade it which can get really boring over the course of hundred hours if your moveset is narrow some items and spells are balanced around pvp instead of solo play which can unintuitively lead to upgrades being downgrades in practice and you wont be able to tell until youve invested lot of resources into unlocking or upgrading them theres also plenty of things to watch out for that will make the game harder if youre not aware of them1 the game is designed for coop the bossfights are tuned to be challenging even when two players are bouncing aggro between them which means that if youre playing solo your summon is part of your build as much as anything else and forgoing it makes things exponentially harder2 the game expects you to explore and level lot if you try to just stick to the critical path to beat it as quickly as possible youre in for rude surprise in its later half of the game due to the sheer amount of damage enemies deal there3 not all builds are made equal your experience will vary lot based on whether you have ranged attack or are going melee only especially since some of the bosses are so big that being in melee range means you cant see their swingsbut all of those arent necessarily shortcomings think of them as an indirect difficulty setting you can go for the easiest approach in each scenario or you can selfimpose challenges for extra thrill its just mindset thing that you have to be aware of going in other than that the game is sublime youll encounter the odd glitch and weird physics interaction here and there but other than that its way more polished that youd expect for the openworld genre

cyberpunk 2077 needs introduction this is the game most of us have been waiting to play for very long time got to sink good amount of hours into this and i am aware that im nowhere near finishing it soon my completionist heart taken over and i want to explore and do every little side activity i can find however i think im ready to express what fantastic breathtaking and imaginative roleplaying game cdpr have managed to create the writing and delivery is step above anything the studio done before with all characters delivering stellar voice performances that are confidently grounded in night cityi mean the world building characters quests music on display are insane its jam packed with cynical and philosophical view on humanity consumerism fuels the economy and megacorporations taring the world apart literally striping humanity to the bone by the addition of cybernatic enhancements that have become the norm this is mean and cruel dystopian hellscape that takes hold and refuses to let go the storytelling in my eyes ventures to places that challenge our views exhibiting all the worse qualities of this battered and broken society which is something that easily be applied to our futurethere is lot to unpack in the first hours the path you choose will not only determine where our mercenary grew up but also how they react to situations throughout night city this leads to multitude of narratives offers depth to your character v who can have different insights or knowledge about certain topics depending on their attributes i went for more of an engineer type character for my first playthrough who is also specialized with handguns so far im having blasti really like the combat in the game while it isnt unique the rpg elements that surround the game offer bit more diversity to how you approach each conflict what i absolutely respect is the decision for firstperson perspective at all times because once you start playing the game you will understand the value to your immersion by having this one preset view for it helps to really be immersed in this universe now my decisions or rather vs decisions make for more compelling experience you can diplomatically defuse situation or pull out your weapon and just blast every scum in your way forcing you to accept whatever consequences might surface as resultits unfortunate the game was launched with so many bugs glitches and poor performance not everyone after number of delays i personally encountered very few bugs and had performance issues for cyberpunk 2077 run smooth all throughout my playthrough as far as im aware many of these issues are predominant on consoles as i am playing this on pc maybe im just lucky flaws aside this is an open world bugs and glitches are to be expected in the first couple of weeks and im very sure cdpr are doing their best to bring out fixes asap but i can understand peoples frustration with thisupdatemonths and months have passed showing the poor state of development this game was in as of now there are numerous issues from performance to more glitches and bugs some added recently from the patches that really stains the overall quality of the gamei had fun playing and finishing cyberpunk 2077 when it released the few bugs encountered were just funny to and did not break the story at any point time passed and im reflecting on many things ive ignored or simply left alone thinking they will be fixed soon it is crystal clear to now why so many people really hated cyberpunk 2077 and while i do disagree with some of them i totally agree with the rest there is very little excuse that this game was released to such degree of unpolished and disregard to the fans i can only hope and wait for cdpr to sink serious time and resources to rectify these mistakesoverall i will recommend the game if you like cyberpunk themed stories and crave good shooter at least on sale
